old: Be careful not to confuse frequentative -gat/-get with causative -tat/-tet: 'olvasgat' means 'he reads casually for himself', whereas 'olvastat' means 'he makes someone else read'.
new: The doer does not change: in 'olvas' and 'olvasgat' the same person reads. The suffix -gat/-get changes only the rhythm of the action (casual, repeated, unhurried).
